title: Hint Oracle: architectural-fingerprint driven prefill/decode autotuner
creator: Aditi Rao
description:
Problem: the serving runtime currently relies on a small set of static heuristics for kernel choice that don’t generalize across heterogeneous GPU families and multimodal sequence-length distributions. This causes suboptimal latency and cost for mixed workloads (short chat queries vs long-document prefill) and makes rollouts risky when new microkernels or quantized variants are introduced.

Proposal: implement a Hint Oracle system — a compact architectural-fingerprint and sequence-length aware registry that recommends an execution plan (kernel variant + batching policy + KV-cache warmstart hint) per request class. The system will combine three sources of signal: 1) fast microbench probes (online microbenchmarks warmed per-GPU), 2) telemetry-derived cost surfaces (empirical latency/cost for ark/kernel combos by seqlen bucket), and 3) a light-weight contextual bandit that selects exploration arms on low-risk windows.

Goals: (a) reduce p95/p99 token latency for decode-heavy workloads by 10% for affected customers, (b) reduce per-token GPU time for long-prefill workflows by 8–15% via better kernel/quantization pairing, and (c) provide safe, auditable rollouts for new kernel variants with automatic fallback to conservative choices on SLA breaches.

Design highlights: 
- Architectural fingerprint: small JSON-like tag computed at model-load time describing device (arch family, sm_version), memory topology, CC capability, and observed occupancy statistics. Stored in Hint Registry keyed by model-version+device-fingerprint.
- Seqlen bucketing: baseline buckets (<=32, 33-128, 129-512, >512) but pluggable to empirical histograms per-customer.
- Microprobe harness: per-GPU short-running microbenchmarks for each candidate kernel (prefill/decoder variants, quantized fallback). Probes prioritize low-overhead sampling (100–500 inferences across short sequences) and run during low-util windows and when new kernels are introduced.
- Bandit controller: constrained Thompson-sampling style controller with a safety layer that enforces latency SLO headroom. Exploration rate is gated by headroom and customer-specific SLO budgets; never explores if headroom < configured threshold.
- Hint Registry API: get_hint(model_version, device_fingerprint, client_profile) -> ordered list of candidate kernels + expected cost estimate + confidence. Hints cached at route level; TTL tunable.
- Observability: per-hint telemetry (invocations, realized latency, cost delta vs baseline), and automatic alerts on regressions. Rollout UI in Console with canary percentages and automatic rollback triggers.

Implementation plan: 1) prototype microprobe harness and a lightweight registry (2 sprints), 2) integrate bandit controller and telemetry pipeline (1 sprint), 3) implement safe rollout and Console controls (1 sprint), 4) customer pilots and gradual ramp (2 sprints).

Security/compliance: no user PII collected by probes; all telemetry uses tokenized IDs and adheres to existing KMS/encryption in flight and at rest.
acceptance_criteria: Hint Registry provides consistent recommendations for at least 95% of model_version+device combinations observed in internal fleet
Microprobe results correlate with full workload latency within +/- 12% for 80% of tested kernels
Bandit controller safely explores new kernels without increasing p99 latency beyond configured SLO headroom in controlled canaries
Console rollout UI exposes per-hint traffic split, rollback, and alerts; PRD and runbook linked
Two customer pilots demonstrate >=8% avg GPU time reduction on long-prefill workloads or equivalent cost savings
steps: Design schema for device fingerprint and seqlen buckets (eng + infra + runtime)
Implement microprobe harness in runtime with opt-in low-priority scheduling
Create Hint Registry service (read-heavy) with per-route caching and TTLs
Build bandit controller library with safety gate and SLO-aware throttler
Hook telemetry: add per-hint metrics, dashboards, and regression alerts
Add Console controls for canary %, manual override, and rollback
Run internal A/B experiments across mixed chat/prefill workloads
Iterate on probe sampling parameters to minimize probe cost and noise
comments: 2026-02-21 — Aditi Rao: initial RFC posted in Confluence (https://redwood.internal/confluence/HintOracle-RFC). Looking for feedback from runtime and infra teams on fingerprint shape.

2026-02-25 — Marco Liu: implemented first microprobe harness prototype in a test branch; microbenchmarks run on a single A100 and an RTX8000. Early result: small kernels beat generic kernel for <=16 seqs but regress at >=512. Recording data in /dashboards/probes/initial-run.

2026-03-01 — Sara Thompson (SRE): flagged potential probe contention on crowded nodes. Suggested we only run probes on spare capacity nodes or within reserved maintenance windows and expose an opt-out via tenant config.
2026-03-05 — Marco Liu: added safety gate to bandit controller — exploration suppressed if node headroom < 20% or p95 slack below 2x target. Unit tests added for gating logic.
2026-03-09 — Product: requested customer pilot candidates (search team and docs ingest team). Prelim pilot plan shared: 2-week canary with 5% traffic, increase to 25% if no regressions.

2026-03-12 — Marco Liu: telemetry pipeline hooked to observability (https://grafana.redwood/runtime/hint_oracle); created dashboard panels for per-hint cost deltas and confidence heatmaps. Next: integrate Console UI controls.
